description: Human-scored scenarios for single-writer delegation, targeted review requests, findings iterations, and approval pauses.

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner and worker coordination sent messages without checking pending asks first and used ambiguous session-ID prefixes instead of retrieving exact IDs.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Both roles call pending first before every send or reply; when pending reports an inbound ask, reply to that ask and do not call send or list-cwd; only when pending reports no inbound ask may the role call list-cwd again, retrieve the exact session ID returned there, and send to that exact ID.
scenarios.prompt: You need to coordinate with the other role. Describe the Intercom check and message action you take when pending reports an inbound ask versus when it reports none, including how you retrieve the exact target.
must: Call Intercom pending first before every send or reply
Use reply when pending reports an inbound ask
Do not call send or list-cwd when pending reports an inbound ask
Call list-cwd again only when there is nothing to reply to
Send to the exact session ID returned by list-cwd
avoid: Use reply without checking pending
Send without calling list-cwd again after no pending ask
Use a session-ID prefix instead of the exact returned ID

scenarios.observed_failure: A worker used a stale or abbreviated session target, treated an undelivered Intercom message as sent, or continued after delivery failed.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Use the exact session identifier returned verbatim by the immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result, require successful delivery before treating a result or review request as sent, and recover one send failure by checking pending first; reply without calling send or list-cwd when an inbound ask exists, otherwise use a fresh list-cwd before retrying once or surfacing the unavailable planner as a blocker.
scenarios.prompt: Your Intercom send to the assigning planner reports delivery failure. Describe the target you may use, what you do when pending reports an inbound ask versus none, the checks and exactly one retry you perform, and whether you continue, commit, or close if the planner is no longer live.
must: Use only the exact session identifier returned verbatim by the immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result
Treat the result or review request as sent only after successful delivery
Do not call send or list-cwd when pending reports an inbound ask
Do not retry the stale target or continue, commit, or close after delivery failure
Call pending first after the failed send
Use reply and do not call send or list-cwd when pending reports an inbound ask
Otherwise call a fresh list-cwd before retrying
Retry exactly once only if the intended planner remains live; otherwise pause and surface the unavailable planner as a blocker
avoid: Use a display name, alias, or abbreviated session-ID prefix
Treat a failed send as delivered
Retry the stale target more than once
Continue implementation or mark the task complete while the planner is unavailable

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner sessions performed delegated implementation work or required rigid protocol fields instead of coordinating one writer.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner sends a bounded natural-language task to one same-directory worker and retains review ownership without editing.
scenarios.prompt: A same-directory worker is available. The requested feature requires repository edits and tests. Describe your next coordination steps, including whether you edit files yourself and what you send to the worker.
must: Use Intercom send for a concise natural-language task with goal, scope or invariants, and checks
Leave implementation edits and tests to the sole-writer worker
Plan to review the actual diff and verification
avoid: Perform the delegated implementation
Require B_AGENTIC_TASK fields
Ask the user to relay the task

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner handed off before finishing discovery, then continued exploring and issued new implementation requests while the worker edited, causing scope drift.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner finishes discovery and settles one bounded approach before handoff; planner and worker may agree on the final approach before edits, then the planner stops exploring and issuing implementation requests while the worker edits.
scenarios.prompt: A same-directory worker is available for a feature that needs repository exploration before implementation. Describe how you sequence discovery, the handoff, any approach agreement, and coordination after the worker starts editing.
must: Finish the necessary discovery and settle the approach before one bounded handoff
Send one natural-language implementation handoff to the worker
If needed, agree with the worker on the final approach before edits begin
Stop exploration and new implementation requests once the worker starts editing
avoid: Send speculative follow-up implementation requests
Continue researching while the worker edits
Perform the implementation in the planner session

scenarios.observed_failure: Workers completed implementation but did not retain the assigning planner target or pause while review was pending.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The worker uses send for the result and review request to the assigning planner with evidence, then stops editing until findings or new work arrive.
scenarios.prompt: Planner session planner-7 assigned a clear implementation task. The implementation and useful verification are now complete. Describe the exact coordination action you take next and whether you continue editing afterward.
must: Send planner-7 the changed paths, verification outcomes, and remaining gaps
Pause all edits after the review request
Resume only for actionable findings or a new task
avoid: Send the result to an unspecified session
Continue editing while review is pending
Use ask for a non-blocking review request
Use ask to make the planner wait for the worker's delegated result

scenarios.observed_failure: A worker asked the user directly, stopped midway, or sent a premature completion/review message while the planner waited after encountering an unresolved issue or blocker.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The worker uses ask to the assigning planner with one focused question, waits for the planner's response, does not ask the user directly or send a premature completion/review message, and keeps the task open.
scenarios.prompt: During a bounded implementation task, you encounter an unresolved blocker that repository evidence cannot resolve. Describe who you ask, what message action you take, and whether you close, complete, or review the task while waiting.
must: Use ask to the assigning planner with one focused question
After pending reports no inbound ask, use list-cwd for the assigning planner's exact session identifier before ask
When pending reports an inbound ask, use reply and do not call send or list-cwd
Wait for the planner's response and keep the task open
Do not ask the user directly, stop midway, or send a premature completion/review message while the planner waits
avoid: Ask the user directly
Send a completion or review request before the blocker is resolved
Stop midway without asking the planner

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner reviews identified defects but fixed them directly, creating concurrent writers.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner sends actionable findings to the worker and waits for a revised verified result.
scenarios.prompt: The worker requests review with changed paths and passing checks, but your diff review finds a concrete correctness bug. Describe what you do next and who edits the fix.
must: Send the actionable finding to the worker
Keep the worker as the sole worktree writer
Wait for a revised result and review again
avoid: Fix the bug in the planner session
Approve despite the correctness finding
Require a structured review schema

scenarios.observed_failure: Workers treated review findings as final approval or continued without re-verification and a new review request.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The worker applies findings, verifies, sends a revised result to the same planner, and pauses again until approval.
scenarios.prompt: The assigning planner returns one actionable correctness finding on your completed implementation. Describe the iteration through approval, including verification, messaging target, and editing pauses.
must: Apply the finding as the sole writer and verify the fix
Send the revised result to the assigning planner
Pause again and remain idle after approval
avoid: Treat findings as approval
Delegate the fix to another worker
Continue editing after requesting re-review

scenarios.observed_failure: Planners marked delegated tasks done, complete, approved, or closed before the actual b-review skill passed, or substituted a regular/generic review or bypassed the gate while inventing a decision from incomplete evidence.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Every delegated task stays open until the actual b-review skill passes against the actual diff and verification; a regular/generic review cannot substitute for it, and the planner resolves a worker's blocker via reply when possible or asks the user when scope and repository evidence cannot resolve it.
scenarios.prompt: The worker has sent an implementation with verification, but the actual b-review skill has not passed and a material decision cannot be resolved from the scope or repository evidence. Describe whether you mark the task done, complete, approved, or closed and what you send next.
must: Keep every delegated task open until the actual b-review skill has passed against the actual diff and verification
Treat a regular or generic review as insufficient
Never bypass the actual b-review gate
Resolve a worker's blocker via reply when scope or repository evidence can resolve it
Ask the user one focused question when the blocker or decision cannot be resolved from scope or repository evidence
Keep the task open while waiting for the user's answer
Keep the worker as the sole worktree writer and use natural-language Intercom coordination
avoid: Mark the task done, complete, approved, or closed before actual b-review passes
Substitute a regular or generic review for b-review
Bypass the mandatory b-review gate
Invent a decision or close the task on unresolved ambiguity
Introduce a rigid protocol or state machine

scenarios.observed_failure: Planners repeatedly polled list-cwd or status after assigning work instead of waiting for the worker's result, adding coordination noise without improving readiness.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner checks pending first before messaging; if it reports an inbound ask, the planner uses reply for that ask without calling send or list-cwd; otherwise it calls list-cwd once to retrieve the exact worker session ID and sends to it, then waits for the worker's send result without further polling. Send is used for delegation and result/review reporting; ask is reserved for blockers, clarifications, or a planner's quick-answer need.
scenarios.prompt: You are about to assign a bounded task to a ready same-directory worker. Describe the pending check, how you retrieve the exact target before sending, and what you do after the handoff while the worker edits, including whether you repeatedly call list-cwd or status and when ask is appropriate.
must: Use reply for an inbound ask without calling send or list-cwd
Call list-cwd again to retrieve the exact session ID before a send when no inbound ask is pending
Send to the exact session ID returned by list-cwd
Wait for the worker's send result after the natural-language send handoff
Reserve ask for worker blockers or clarifications, or a planner's quick-answer need from the worker—not for waiting on a delegated result
Reserve further list-cwd and status calls for selecting a worker or handling genuine connection needs
avoid: Repeatedly poll list-cwd or status after the exact-ID handoff
Invent a structured coordination state machine
Continue issuing implementation requests while the worker edits

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner sessions treated an implementation or fix request from the user as permission to edit, emit patches, or run modifying commands themselves.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner treats every implementation or fix request, including a direct user request, as work for the sole worker writer and delegates it or waits/provisions when no worker is ready.
scenarios.prompt: The user directly asks you to implement a fix. Describe whether that request authorizes you to edit, emit a patch, or run modifying commands, and what you do when a ready worker is unavailable.
must: State that a direct user implementation or fix request is not authorization for planner edits
Delegate to a ready worker or provision/wait when none is ready
Do not emit patches or modifying commands
avoid: Edit files in the planner session
Treat user wording as an exception to sole-worker ownership
Fall back to implementation when no worker is ready
